curriculum.lesson_evidence: Slow breathing and gentle stretching tell the body it is safe to relax. In belly breathing you breathe in slowly through the nose while the belly rises, then out slowly through the mouth, repeated several times. A gentle stretch is held without bouncing and stopped if anything hurts. Do these in a clear space and only at your own comfortable level; sitting versions are just as good.

lesson.child_mission: Slow breathing and gentle stretching tell the body it is safe to relax. In belly breathing you breathe in slowly through the nose while the belly rises, then out slowly through the mouth, repeated several times. A gentle stretch is held without bouncing and stopped if anything hurts. Do these in a clear space and only at your own comfortable level; sitting versions are just as good.

lesson.extension: Apply the same idea to a new game or situation, then compare two choices for safety and inclusion.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
A friend breathes in fast and loudly when upset. Write the steps you would tell them for belly breathing and for one safe stretch, including when to stop.

FEEDBACK
Steps: sit comfortably with a hand on the belly, breathe in slowly through the nose so the belly rises, out slowly through the mouth, repeat five times. Stretch: reach up tall and hold without bouncing. Stop if it hurts or you feel dizzy, then sit and breathe normally.

WATCH FOR
Thinking a stretch should hurt to work, or that breathing fast and deep is calming. Calming breaths are slow and gentle, and stretches should feel comfortable, never painful.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.

teaching.why: This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.
